title: Introduce verifiable response protocol and schema handshake for streaming tool calls
author: Aisha K. Patel
release_notes: Adds a verifiable response protocol (VRP) that negotiates a schema handshake for streamed responses and tool calls. Introduces incremental validation checkpoints, new error codes for schema/stream/tool failures, and a per-route strictness toggle (opt-in rollout).
description:
Context: Customers using structured output with streaming have experienced silent schema drift and partial tool invocations being forwarded when the model output is invalid. This PR implements a verifiable response protocol (VRP) and schema handshake to give callers deterministic behavior for structured outputs, plus safer tool/function calling semantics and improved OpenAI-compat error mapping. Motivation: reduce customer incidents caused by malformed streaming JSON and ensure tool calls are only executed after an explicit handshake when schema constraints apply. Goals: 1) Provide a wire-level handshake that lets the server accept/convert/decline a requested response_format/schema; 2) Validate streams incrementally with lightweight checkpoints to allow mid-stream recovery/resume; 3) Fence tool/function calls until the model output has passed a minimal schema gate; 4) Expose clear error codes for API consumers and map them to OpenAI-compat shapes when using the compatibility layer; 5) Make strict validation opt-in per-route so we can rollout safely.

What changed (high level): - Introduces a VRP layer that negotiates response_format + schema version at request start. The server can respond with an accepted schema variant or an explicit negotiation rejection with reasons. - Adds incremental validation checkpoints in the streaming path. Each checkpoint emits a small signed resume token that the client can use to resume validation-aware streams when transient failures occur. Checkpoints are lightweight and intended not to increase per-token latency significantly. - Adds a toolcall fencing mechanism: tool invocation events are withheld from the tool-executor until the VRP gate for the required structured fields reaches a configurable minimal confidence/validation state. This prevents partial/malformed payloads from reaching backend tooling. - Extends OpenAI compatibility mapper to translate VRP-specific errors into OpenAI-compatible error objects (error.type, error.code, error.param) so clients using the OpenAI shape get meaningful, actionable diagnostics. - Config and rollout: a new per-route config vrp.strict_mode: off|permissive|strict. By default routes remain permissive; strict must be enabled by customer or rolled out by feature flag. - Metrics/tracing: new metrics vrp.validation.ok, vrp.validation.fail, vrp.stream.resume_count, vrp.tool.fenced_count and tracing spans for handshake/validation checkpoints. - Documentation: docs/openapi/response_format.md and examples/strict-mode-rollout.md added.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4527) - [x] Unit tests for handshake and checkpoint parsing - [x] Integration test for toolcall fencing - [x] OpenAI-compat mappings covered by contract tests - [x] Feature flag and rollout plan in examples/strict-mode-rollout.md - [x] Observability events emitted

Review conversation:
- Diego Morales: "Can we make the checkpoint signature size configurable? I worry about payload bloat for short lived sessions." (requested change)
- Aisha (author): "Added config.max_checkpoint_sig_bytes to vrp_config.yaml and made default small (96 bytes). Tests updated to simulate truncation." (author reply)
- Rina Sato: "Toolcall fence looks good but we should bubble a non-500 error to callers when a tool is intentionally withheld." (requested change)
- Aisha: "Changed fence behavior: it now returns a VRP_TOOL_FENCED user-visible error (4xx-like in OpenAI-compat) and emits a trace span so operator tooling can correlate." (author reply)
- Evan Liu: "Performance baseline looked acceptable in local canary; please include a rollout note about CPU footprint." (comment)
- Aisha: "Added perf numbers to examples/strict-mode-rollout.md and added a disabled perf test that can be re-enabled during canaries." (author reply)
- Diego Morales: "Approving pending CI green and small nit about variable name in checkpoint.rs" (approved after nit fixed)

Observability and rollout notes: - Default behavior is permissive; customers won't see changes unless they enable vrp.strict_mode or request strict via API. - Recommend staged rollout: enable on 1% traffic with onboarding test prompts, then 10%, then full. - Watch vrp.validation.fail and vrp.tool.fenced_count; set alert if fenced_count grows unexpectedly after enabling strict.

Backward compatibility: - Non-VRP clients (no response_format/schema) are unaffected. - OpenAI-compat mapping preserves existing shapes for existing errors; new error codes are added but mapped to OpenAI type/param so clients can handle them.

Merge: merged by Rina Sato using squash and merge. See changelog entry for VRP handshake in release notes.

example_calls: POST /v1/responses with response_format={schema:v3} returns VRP handshake and resume tokens
Client can retry stream with ?resume_token=<token> to continue validation-aware stream
